From 41b145024ca717254bb6882f1312299db958bf0c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jacob Keller <jacob.e.keller@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2020 14:08:35 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mlx4: fix "initializer element not constant" compiler error
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

A recent commit e8937681797c ("devlink: prepare to support region
operations") used the region_cr_space_str and region_fw_health_str
variables as initializers for the devlink_region_ops structures.

This can result in compiler errors:
drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox//mlx4/crdump.c:45:10: error: initializer
element is not constant
   .name = region_cr_space_str,
           ^
drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox//mlx4/crdump.c:45:10: note: (near
initialization for ‘region_cr_space_ops.name’)
drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox//mlx4/crdump.c:50:10: error: initializer
element is not constant
   .name = region_fw_health_str,

The variables were made to be "const char * const", indicating that both
the pointer and data were constant. This was enough to resolve this on
recent GCC (gcc (GCC) 9.2.1 20190827 (Red Hat 9.2.1-1) for this author).

Unfortunately this is not enough for older compilers to realize that the
variable can be treated as a constant expression.

Fix this by introducing macros for the string and use those instead of
the variable name in the region ops structures.

Reported-by: tanhuazhong <tanhuazhong@huawei.com>
Fixes: e8937681797c ("devlink: prepare to support region operations")
Signed-off-by: Jacob Keller <jacob.e.keller@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/crdump.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/crdump.c
index 2700628f1689..73eae80e1cb7 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/crdump.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/crdump.c
@@ -38,16 +38,19 @@
 #define CR_ENABLE_BIT_OFFSET		0xF3F04
 #define MAX_NUM_OF_DUMPS_TO_STORE	(8)
 
-static const char * const region_cr_space_str = "cr-space";
-static const char * const region_fw_health_str = "fw-health";
+#define REGION_CR_SPACE "cr-space"
+#define REGION_FW_HEALTH "fw-health"
+
+static const char * const region_cr_space_str = REGION_CR_SPACE;
+static const char * const region_fw_health_str = REGION_FW_HEALTH;
 
 static const struct devlink_region_ops region_cr_space_ops = {
-	.name = region_cr_space_str,
+	.name = REGION_CR_SPACE,
 	.destructor = &kvfree,
 };
 
 static const struct devlink_region_ops region_fw_health_ops = {
-	.name = region_fw_health_str,
+	.name = REGION_FW_HEALTH,
 	.destructor = &kvfree,
 };
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `crdump.c`**
1. Removed the initialization of the variables `region_cr_space_str` and `region_fw_health_str` as string constants.
2. Introduced two macros: `REGION_CR_SPACE` defined as "cr-space" and `REGION_FW_HEALTH` defined as "fw-health".
3. Updated the definitions of `region_cr_space_str` and `region_fw_health_str` to use the newly defined macros.
4. Updated the `name` fields in the `region_cr_space_ops` and `region_fw_health_ops` structures to use the macros instead of the variable names.

### Relationships
The modifications in `crdump.c` were addressed to resolve a compiler error related to "initializer element not constant." The previous version of the code was utilizing string variables as initializers for structures, which caused issues with certain compilers. By replacing those variables with macros, the code maintains the intended constant values while ensuring compatibility with older compilers, effectively eliminating the reported compilation errors.

Reported-by: tanhuazhong <tanhuazhong@huawei.com>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is the use of variables (`region_cr_space_str` and `region_fw_health_str`) as initializers for the `devlink_region_ops` structures, which older compilers do not treat as constant expressions. This results in compiler errors indicating that the initializer elements are not constant. The variables, despite being defined as `const char * const`, were still not recognized as constant expressions by some compilers, leading to compilation failures.

Here is the patch:
 #define MAX_NUM_OF_DUMPS_TO_STORE	(8)
 
-static const char * const region_cr_space_str = "cr-space";
-static const char * const region_fw_health_str = "fw-health";
+#define REGION_CR_SPACE "cr-space"
+#define REGION_FW_HEALTH "fw-health"
+
+static const char * const region_cr_space_str = REGION_CR_SPACE;
+static const char * const region_fw_health_str = REGION_FW_HEALTH;
 
 static const struct devlink_region_ops region_cr_space_ops = {
-	.name = region_cr_space_str,
+	.name = REGION_CR_SPACE,
 	.destructor = &kvfree,
 };
 
 static const struct devlink_region_ops region_fw_health_ops = {
-	.name = region_fw_health_str,
+	.name = REGION_FW_HEALTH,
 	.destructor = &kvfree,
 };

```c
-static const char * const region_fw_health_str = "fw-health";
```
Reason:
The variables `region_cr_space_str` and `region_fw_health_str` are used as initializers for the `devlink_region_ops` structures. Older compilers do not recognize these variables, even though they are defined as `const`, as constant expressions, leading to compiler errors indicating that the initializer elements are not constant.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+#define REGION_CR_SPACE "cr-space"
+#define REGION_FW_HEALTH "fw-health"
```
Reason:
By introducing macros `REGION_CR_SPACE` and `REGION_FW_HEALTH`, the code uses these macros as initializers for the `devlink_region_ops` structures instead of the variables. Macros are treated as constant expressions by all compilers, thus resolving the compilation errors.
